extracted.intended_audience: authors, publishers, translators, and literary professionals interested in submitting to or learning about the National Book Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Information and high-level criteria for the National Book Awards program, including which categories are honored, where to find eligibility and submission rules, and available medallions/rights for honored titles. Useful for prospective submitters and publishers preparing entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The Awards currently honor the best Fiction, Nonfiction, Poetry, Translated Literature, and Young People’s Literature, published each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the distinct genres/categories for which titles are considered; prospective submitters should map their book to one of these categories. (The page references that other categories have been recognized historically but the current set is these five.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines & Guidelines (eligibility and submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility, the submissions process, current prizes, guidelines, FAQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page references a Deadlines & Guidelines section for concrete rules (eligibility criteria, submission procedures, prize amounts, and FAQs). Specific eligibility rules and deadlines are not included on this page and must be consulted via the linked guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medallions and digital image rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Seals and digital image rights are available for NBA Winner, Finalist, and Longlist titles. In addition to medallions for individual titles, we also offer medallions for 5 Under 35 honorees and Distinguished Contribution to American Letters medalists, which can be used for future or backlist titles, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winners/finalists/longlisted titles (and specified honorees) may use official seals and obtain digital image rights; publishers should follow the Foundation's rules for usage (details are available via the linked Medallions page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program purpose and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Established in 1950 to celebrate the best writing in America. Since 1989, they have been overseen by the National Book Foundation, a nonprofit organization whose mission is to celebrate the best of American literature, to expand its audience, and to enhance the cultural value of great writing in America.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statement frames the Awards' evaluative intent (celebrating 'the best writing in America') and institutional oversight; it implies selection is focused on literary merit within American publishing but does not provide concrete judging criteria on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ceremony and current awards year
rubrics_metrics.description: Current Awards Year — 2022 National Book Awards. The 73rd National Book Awards Ceremony will be broadcast live on November 16, 2022 at 8:00pm ET.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Logistical/temporal information about the awards cycle and public ceremony; relevant for timing submissions and publicity but not a judging standard. The site provides a way to sign up for updates and watch the ceremony live.
